# ai.market Runbooks

This repository is the maintained discovery corpus for ai.market system-level
runbooks. `ACTIVE` means structurally admitted to the integrity-only catalog; it
does not mean that an operational claim has been semantically verified or may
authorize an action. Grandfathered documents remain readable only by explicit
Git path.

## Catalog scope

The live catalog has one membership state: `ACTIVE`. Legacy Gate-1-through-4
adoption labels no longer drive selection. A Markdown document without ACTIVE
catalog metadata is grandfathered source material, readable only by explicit
path. The legacy metadata names `authoritative_for` for compatibility, but the
catalog v2 envelope and every entry explicitly carry `integrity_only: true`,
`semantic_verification: false`, `authority_admission: false`, and
`action_authority_eligible: false`.

Files under `archive/` are recoverable historical evidence, not instructions.
Never execute a command from an archived file without revalidating it against
the owning current runbook and live ground truth.

Corpus discovery is fail closed: Markdown in a new or unknown directory enters
adjudication automatically. Only the root generated README/router, enumerated
top-level `archive/`, `audits/`, `contracts/`, `specs/`, `templates/`, and
`tests/` trees, and named dependency/cache trees are excluded. Admitted file or
directory symlinks are rejected rather than followed.

## Working on a runbook

- Before planning, use one immutable full-SHA catalog snapshot for every objective. When context delivery is active, the first `kd_session_plan` response supplies that server-verified pin and ranked excerpts before the plan can become operational. During the bounded legacy rollout only, resolve a freshly fetched `origin/main` in a trusted clean checkout, record the missing automatic delivery as rollout evidence, and run `python -m runbook_tools.catalog search --catalog-ref git:aidotmarket/runbooks@<full-sha>:CATALOG.json "<objective>"` from the repository root (`runbook-catalog` is the installed equivalent); never invent or reuse an unverified pin.
- Search several objectives against that same immutable snapshot by repeating `--query` with `python -m runbook_tools.catalog search-many`. Single and batch output are capped at 40,000 UTF-8 bytes (and 40,000 characters). `--limit` caps ID-eligible ACTIVE candidates; supplemental README guidance does not consume that limit. Packing first allocates one fitting eligible candidate per positive objective, then pinned supplemental guidance when applicable, and finally eligible depth round-robin. Guidance can use only capacity left after complete eligible breadth and can never replace an eligible candidate. `serialized_bytes` is the exact size of the CLI JSON line, including its trailing newline. `complete: true` means the returned envelope is intact; intentional omissions are reported by `response_budget_truncated` and `dropped_candidate_count`.
- Create a non-authoritative DRAFT under `runbooks/`: `runbook-new <runbook-id> --owner <owner> --domain <domain>`
- Replace every placeholder with grounded content. A strict §K `yaml promotion-evidence` block conforming to `schemas/runbook_promotion_evidence.schema.json` may record preparatory claim/evidence candidates and explicit visible `UNKNOWN` gaps. Free text, section mappings, exact blob identity, tests written by the same author, and the corpus ledger's `verify_against` list are not semantic verification or authority.
- `runbook-catalog pin-evidence <runbook-id>` mechanically fills Git-blob and SHA-256 digests for preparatory code/test/schema/spec/workflow locators. It keeps the file DRAFT and cannot authorize promotion. If retained for future receipt work, commit the DRAFT and cited sources, add its non-authoritative pending ledger record, then refresh `CORPUS-MANIFEST.yaml` from that exact content commit.
- `runbook-catalog promote <runbook-id>` is unavailable for every risk class in this snapshot. Trusted claim-bound evidence plus independent review authority is not deployed, so an author-supplied receipt ID/file, reviewer name, unsigned payload, local test, or `UNKNOWN` decoration cannot pass. The future signed receipt shape is `schemas/runbook_promotion_receipt.schema.json`; it intentionally contains no local key or trust pin.
- Manually changing DRAFT to ACTIVE does not bypass the closure. Every Git repository must contain the exact immutable rollout commit `a6d7534a35d921138c139bdf69aaeddd0faec100`; generation `HEAD` and every pinned validation SHA must descend from it under `git --no-replace-objects`. Catalog v2 then requires the exact 20-ID population and the byte-digest-pinned reviewed projection in `schemas/legacy_catalog_projection.policy.json`: IDs, explicitly approved canonical path moves, topics, sections and stable section IDs, aliases, error signatures, and supersession fields are frozen. Any other repository/history, missing member, new ID/topic/signature/alias, unreviewed path, dirty policy bytes, or replacement-ref trick fails closed. Existing content changes remain assist/shadow material only and cannot create semantic or action authority.
- Validate a runbook: `runbook-lint <path>`
- After committing source or archive changes, mechanically refresh the ledger from that exact content commit: `python -m runbook_tools.corpus_manifest --refresh-from <full-content-commit-sha>`. The SHA must equal checked-out `HEAD`; the command changes only derived paths, blob IDs, counts, and the inventory pin, validates a temporary candidate, then replaces the canonical ledger atomically. A repository lock plus optimistic compare-and-swap refuses concurrent evidence edits. It never invents or changes adjudication, risk, evidence, or disposition fields.
- Validate the complete source estate and its pinned Git inventory: `python -m runbook_tools.corpus_manifest`. `CORPUS-MANIFEST.yaml` is a pending adjudication ledger, not authority; every source edit or move must refresh its declared blob and inventory snapshot.
- Before enabling blocking enforcement, run `python -m runbook_tools.corpus_manifest --promotion-bar`. It fails while trusted claim-bound evidence and independent review authority are unavailable, while any pending source remains, any source document is outside `runbooks/`, any surviving source is not ACTIVE, or an ACTIVE ledger row lacks evidence. Existing ACTIVE files remain available only as the explicit legacy shadow set; catalog syntax and local evidence are not truth certificates.
- Run the retired LLM exam only as an explicit diagnostic: `runbook-harness --runbook <path>`; its score is not freshness or conformance evidence

Automatic catalog-based lint and harness modes print the selected target paths
and fail when they select zero targets. Staleness age and escalation are owned
by canonical server state; agents cannot create or reset that clock by editing a
runbook.

Search results are candidates for inspection, not truth certificates:

- `candidates_returned_unverified` means the retriever found one or more relevant ACTIVE sections. Read the excerpt and verify load-bearing facts against their owning code, live schema, configuration, or state before relying on them.
- `no_positive_candidate_in_active_catalog` is an honest retrieval miss, not proof that no runbook exists. Record/use the gateway-issued gap path and broaden discovery without inventing a citation.
- `no_usable_candidate_id_response_budget` means a batch objective had positive candidates but none fit after the breadth-first allocation. It is a non-success with no usable candidate ID: retry in a smaller batch or keep the future gateway plan non-operational.
- `repository_authoring_guidance` is pinned supplemental context for a clause-local authoring action applied to a documentation artifact. It is returned only after eligible ACTIVE breadth, with `candidate_id_eligible: false`; disconnected mentions and artifacts used as adjectives do not trigger it. `eligible_candidate_count`, `eligible_candidates_returned`, and the separate limit/budget omission counts make every eligible pool disposition explicit.
- `integrity_status: integrity_pass_unverified` and `integrity_only: true` mean only that the bytes and catalog projection passed deterministic integrity checks. `semantic_verification`, `authority_admission`, and `action_authority_eligible` remain `false`: no search candidate authorizes action or proves its operational claims true.
- `catalog_declared`, `declaration_kinds`, and `authority_keys` report whether catalog metadata explicitly points to that exact section. `owner` and `last_verified_at` are source metadata, not independent proof that every excerpt claim is current.
- `excerpt_start_line`, `excerpt_end_line`, `excerpt_end_column_exclusive`, and `excerpt_sha256` make the bounded excerpt reconstructable from the pinned Git blob. `candidate_digest` binds candidate identity; the top-level `delivery_digest` binds the complete response payload.
- Explicit `<!-- catalog:historical -->` spans are excluded from current search and conformance forms. Grandfathered documents remain reachable only by an explicit path and carry no catalog authority.

The validator's `integrity_pass_unverified` status proves only that a full SHA
names a self-consistent Git snapshot descended from the rollout baseline and
matching the frozen legacy discovery projection. The session gateway is the
target authority for supplying an approved `origin/main` pin and binding
consultation/gap identifiers to the session. The manual legacy-rollout fallback
above is diagnostic and temporary, never authority for a caller-minted
consultation receipt.

The remaining B0 dependency is external: deploy a gateway-controlled,
claim-bound evidence verifier and independent-review authority bound to the
exact candidate digest, with a pinned trusted validator/schema/projection
package digest plus freshness and revocation checks. Until that complete path exists, promotion,
semantic verification, authority admission, and action-authority eligibility
remain false.

## Tooling

This repository ships `runbook-tools`, a Python package providing:
- `runbook-catalog` / `python -m runbook_tools.catalog` — installed and clean-checkout entry points that generate, validate, resolve, and deterministically search the SHA-pinned legacy catalog; `pin-evidence` is preparatory only and `promote` is fail-closed until trusted authority is deployed
- `runbook-lint` — validates strict-YAML forms and deterministic runbook invariants; normal CI is read-only
- `runbook-new` — generates a DRAFT scaffold that has no catalog authority until promotion
- `runbook-harness` — retains the old stateless-agent exam as a manual diagnostic, never as an automatic compliance writer
- `python -m runbook_tools.corpus_manifest` — prevents the 101-source-document estate plus recoverable archive records, classifications, and pinned blob evidence from silently drifting; use `--refresh-from <full-content-commit-sha>` only after that exact content commit is checked out, while `--promotion-bar` is the later blocking-rollout check

Installation: `pip install -e .` (Python 3.11+).

Current contracts: `specs/RUNBOOK-ORGANIZATION-PLAN-S1387.md` for runbook-first discovery/gates and `specs/BQ-RUNBOOK-STANDARD.md` for document structure and deterministic linting. Historical Gate-2 specifications remain provenance only.
